fields.v: Spec Growth Engine (author's own; open-source implementation: engine, CLI, cockpit, Apache 2.0, github.com/grabow/spec-growth-engine); version Not stated. Kiro, Spec Kit, Tessl discussed only as related work

One SPEC.md per architectural node (C4 levels system/container/component/code), each with a Contract (public interfaces, invariants, types, error behaviour, acceptance criteria) and a Design (internal approach, children, code ownership, constraints); one transversal ARCHITECTURE.md (Layer-1 invariants, principles, ADRs, security policies, naming); derived (not hand-written) index, dependency graph, drift report; Capability Registry (cap:<name> -> one provider); short front-matter headers in source files

Two-layer growth: Layer 1 invariants specified up front; Layer 2 features as hardest-first vertical slices. Per feature: 1 Select story/target node (Planner proposal); 2 run growth rules (6 rules) to update minimal specs; 3 assemble context deterministically (Spine: root invariants + spine contracts + node spec + dependency contracts + own code); 4 Implement (code + same-commit spec delta); 5 Validate (drift check Intent Graph vs Evidence Graph); 6 Gate (HARD/SOFT/AUTO); 7 Update spec graph (index regenerated)

Human Architect approves outward-surface changes: HARD gate (root invariant change, new container boundary, breaking contract change) before merge; SOFT gate (new component, additive contract change) asynchronous review; AUTO gate no human (internal design, refactoring). Human reviews only contract-level lines of the agent's spec delta
Not run, document-based (worked example traced on paper)

Requires a static dependency graph derivable from source (imports, routes, events); highly dynamic systems (runtime DI, plugins) need explicit annotation of late-bound dependencies; governance gate overhead real for fast-moving teams (SOFT gate mitigates). No empirical evaluation reported (implementation in companion paper arXiv:2610.11725)

Inconsistencies: the introduction lists Tessl among spec-first frameworks ('Spec-first frameworks (e.g. AWS Kiro [1], Tessl)', p. 1), while Table 5 and the related work place Tessl at spec-anchored / spec-as-source (p. 12); paper organisation mentions Sections 9-10 but skips 7-8 in the outline. Context-degradation figures (Dumb Zone 40% fill heuristic, LongCodeBench 29%->3%) cited as motivation, flagged by the author as heuristic. Implementation and method documents available (Apache 2.0, GitHub link). No pre-registration. Programming language: N/A (language-agnostic, static import analysis)
